title_en: Forest resilience of Armenia, enhancing adaptation and rural green growth via mitigation (FAO/GCF, GCP/ARM/008/GCF)
implementers: Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU), State Agency of the Ministry of Environment
budget_original: GCF grant USD 10,000,000 + co-financing USD 8,704,730 = USD 18.7 million total (GCF project page SAP014)
cofinancing_note: Co-financing USD 8,704,730 (in-kind and grant) from Government of Armenia, ADA, FAO, WWF Armenia and Autonomous Province of Bolzano.
summary_en: FAO and Armenia's Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU) implement this eight-year Green Climate Fund project in the two marzes with the highest forest degradation, Lori and Syunik. It aims to raise forest cover by 2.5 percent, cut rural fuelwood demand by at least 30 percent, and give communities a larger role in forest and natural-resource governance. The project also sets up forest nurseries and supports the national forest monitoring and assessment system.
activities_en: Climate-adaptive afforestation, reforestation and sustainable forest management with Hayantar SNCO
Forest nurseries (Hrazdan and Sisian) with seed cold-storage facilities
Community-led forest concessions and natural-resource governance
Fuelwood efficiency: improved woodstove design and national energy-efficiency standards
Updating forestry and climate curricula at universities and vocational schools
Support to the National Forest Monitoring and Assessment (NFMA) system
results_en: 103 ha afforested, 10 demonstration plots set up, over 570,000 seedlings produced (FAO fact sheet, 22 Oct 2025)
Four national energy-efficiency standards adopted (target was one)
Collect Earth survey of Armenian land categories completed; 100% of Year-1 and 50% of Year-2 NFMA field data collected

title_en: Fueling Green Recovery in Armenia - advancing forest infrastructure and creating sustainable jobs for rural communities (GCF SAP059)
implementers: Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU), State Agency of the Ministry of Environment (accredited and executing entity)
budget_original: GCF grant USD 9,493,842 + in-kind co-financing USD 506,151 = USD 10.0 million (GCF project page SAP059)
cofinancing_note: USD 506,151 in-kind from Government of Armenia.
summary_en: EPIU implements a five-year Green Climate Fund project to expand national forest-seedling infrastructure and plant new forest in eight marzes that are not covered by the FAO/GCF forest resilience project. It aims to supply 20 million seedlings a year by 2030, establish about 1,300 ha of forest in mountain areas and create about 3,500 green jobs for vulnerable rural people. Hayantar SNCO, Armenia Tree Project and My Forest Armenia are the implementing partners named in the funding proposal.
activities_en: Seed bank and greenhouses under Hayantar SNCO (one 1,000 m2 greenhouse in each beneficiary marz), plus greenhouses at Armenia Tree Project and My Forest Armenia
About 1,000 household backyard seedling nurseries in vulnerable municipalities
Establishment of around 1,300 ha of forest (about 4 million trees) on 120 mapped plots of 3-40 ha in about 50 municipalities
Non-timber forest product value chains and agroforestry; 3,500 sustainable jobs target
Digital monitoring (MRV) and investment platform for forest restoration

title_en: Scaling up national adaptive capacities for climate change-driven natural hazards through strengthening monitoring and early warning systems (GCF SAP068)
implementers: Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU), State Agency of the Ministry of Environment (accredited entity)
budget_original: GCF grant USD 9,499,990 + in-kind co-financing USD 500,000 = USD 10.0 million (GCF project page SAP068)
summary_en: EPIU is the accredited entity for a Green Climate Fund project to build a people-centred, national multi-hazard early warning system for Armenia. It modernises meteorological and hydrological observation and forecasting, strengthens multi-channel early-warning dissemination, and develops resilience-financing tools such as forecast-based financing and climate micro-insurance. The GCF page targets about 1.07 million direct beneficiaries.
activities_en: Modernise meteorological and hydrological observation and forecasting systems
Multi-channel early-warning dissemination and risk communication, including inclusive warnings for about 300,000 vulnerable people
Resilience-financing mechanisms: forecast-based financing and climate micro-insurance

locations.evidence: GCF project page SAP068 lists Armenia as the location; no marz, community or station sites are named.

title_en: Implementation of Armenia's LDN commitments through sustainable land management and restoration of degraded landscapes (FAO/GEF, GCP/ARM/010/GFF)
donors: Government of Armenia and other co-financiers (USD 12,018,000 co-financing)
implementers: Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU), Ministry of Environment (executing partner)
national_partners: Ministry of Territorial Administration and Infrastructure
budget_original: GEF grant USD 2,183,105 + co-financing USD 12,018,000 = USD 14,201,105 total (ProDoc and GEF portal; GEF agency fee USD 207,395 extra)
cofinancing_note: USD 12,018,000 co-financing, including the FAO/GCF forest resilience project that works in the same marzes.
summary_en: This FAO-implemented, GEF-financed project helps Armenia meet its national Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) targets. It works at national level on policy, LDN monitoring and capacity, and on the ground in two landscapes: Sisian (former Gorayk) community in Syunik and Tumanyan community in Lori, where it supports restoration of degraded grassland and cropland, forest restoration (jointly with the FAO/GCF project) and land-based value chains such as dairy, honey, berries and organic vegetables.
activities_en: Strengthen enabling environment: LDN integrated in policies and law, intersectoral coordination mechanism
Map land-degradation trends and drivers, set LDN baselines and targets in Lori and Syunik (Trends.Earth, Collect Earth)
Participatory integrated land-management plans in target communities and 'LDN learning landscapes'
Restore degraded grassland and cropland; forest restoration with FAO/GCF co-financing
Strengthen two land-based value chains (at least one focused on women) and update university curricula
Monitoring system for LDN indicators and UNCCD reporting
results_en: Planned targets (ProDoc): 4,000 ha degraded grassland restored; 7,300 ha forest land restored (co-financing); 166,000 ha under SLM (110,000 forest, 50,000 grassland, 6,000 cropland); 2,500 beneficiaries

Reported to date (UN Armenia): about 300 ha degraded arable land improved in Tumanyan and Sisian (sainfoin, alfalfa, grains); 34,000 vegetable seedlings distributed; 120 beehives, first honey harvest Aug-Sep 2024

notes: Pilot landscapes confirmed by two independent public sources (Panorama.am, Hetq) and by the ProDoc (Lori and Syunik). The five Tumanyan villages (Ahnidzor, Atan, Karinj, Lorut, Shamut) come from the GEF IATI location list and the ProDoc's list of community pasture associations; Tumanyan municipality contains exactly these plus Marts, Kober kayaran and the town (8 settlements, matching Ecolur's '8 settlements'). In Syunik no village list was found; only Sisian/Gorayk community. UN Armenia also mentions Dsegh community in Lori (a farmer profile), not confirmed as a project site. Hetq (Aug 2026) reports conflicting ministry hectare figures (404.3 ha arable, 420 ha pastures) and says the ministry would not say where work was done; those figures are not used. Hetq also describes a 'second phase' to 30 Sep 2027 on forest sustainability in Lori/Syunik, which could not be tied to a separate donor activity. Outputs, targets and the association list come from the project's ProDoc (project document), which has no public URL; the public sources are listed above.

title_en: RESILAND: Armenia Resilient Landscapes Project (World Bank P179988 / GEF 11046)
donors: Sweden / Sida (USD 3.65 million grant, SEK 47 million)
implementers: Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU), Ministry of Environment
budget_original: GEF USD 5.45 million + Sweden USD 3.65 million grants (World Bank press release, 8 May 2024). GEF portal lists total co-financing USD 30,466,278. No total project cost was confirmed on an opened page.
cofinancing_note: GEF portal: total co-financing USD 30,466,278; Sweden contribution of SEK 47 million over about five years (Openaid.se).
summary_en: The World Bank-supported RESILAND project, executed by EPIU, restores fragmented forests, degraded wetlands and abandoned mining sites in four marzes and builds the policy and institutional framework for landscape management. It also supports community forestry, non-timber forest products and ecotourism as alternative incomes. The GEF-side documentation targets improved land condition on 25,800 ha.
activities_en: Policy review and institutional capacity for integrated landscape management
Landscape restoration: forest restoration (rebuilding fragmented forests), wetland restoration and mining-site restoration
Community benefits: community-based forestry management and ecotourism development
Project management, monitoring, evaluation and communication

title_en: Conservation and Sustainable Management of Land Resources and High Value Ecosystems in Lake Sevan Basin for Multiple Benefits (UNDP/GEF 10854)
implementers: Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU), Ministry of Environment (implementing partner)

summary_en: UNDP, with EPIU and WWF Armenia, implements this GEF project to promote land degradation neutrality and secure biodiversity in the Lake Sevan basin. Demonstration sites are in six consolidated communities in Gegharkunik and Vayots Dzor, with restoration of about 2,200 ha of degraded forest land and stronger management of Sevan National Park.

Secure critical habitats for biodiversity services (including Sevan National Park management)
Biodiversity-friendly economic development and incentives for local communities
Restore about 2,200 ha of degraded forest land in coordination with the State Forestry Committee
Knowledge management, monitoring and evaluation

Demonstration and pilot restoration sites with indigenous fruit and nut tree species in communal and degraded areas

title_en: Mainstreaming Sustainable Land and Forest Management in Mountain Landscapes of North-Eastern Armenia (UNDP/GEF 5353; GEF title: '...in Dry Mountain Landscapes')
national_partners: Ministry of Nature Protection (now Ministry of Environment)
budget_original: GEF grant USD 2,977,169 + co-financing USD 13,989,935 = USD 16,967,104 (GEF portal). The project's final-workshop page quotes 'total budget USD 3,157,169', which appears to be the UNDP/GEF grant side only.

summary_en: UNDP/GEF project in Lori and Tavush marzes, which hold about 65 percent of Armenia's forest resources. It integrated sustainable forest and land management into planning across about 650,000 ha, revised forest management plans, rehabilitated pastures and forests in pilot communities and supported alternative livelihoods and energy for forest-dependent villages.

Community-based pasture and fodder improvement and forest-pasture management in six target communities
Forest regeneration, school forest district and sustainable non-timber use (Koghb, Noyemberyan)
Alternative livelihoods and energy (e.g. solar systems at schools and kindergartens, anti-hail stations, efficient stoves)
Dendrochronology and carbon-stock inventory to support national GHG accounting
results_en: 227 ha under fodder production or improved in the six target communities (Regional Post)

Planning/targets reported in 2017: restoration of degraded forest, about 1,000 ha pastures, about 200,000 ha with improved soil management (Ecolur; the article's headline and body disagree on the forest figure)

Final workshop (6-7 May 2021) presented forest-regeneration results, biofuel market development, alternative livelihoods in Tavush, monitoring of illegal deforestation, dendrochronology and carbon stock inventory with national coefficients

donors: Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC)
budget_original: Phase 1 total CHF 2.5 million (CHF 1.5 m economic development + CHF 1.0 m environmental infrastructure and natural-resource management), per Ecolur 28 Nov 2025. SDC approved CHF 4.5 million in principle in 2021 for an eight-year programme.
summary_en: SDC-funded project implemented by WWF Armenia to raise incomes of farmers and rural businesses in remote mountain communities while protecting natural resources and biodiversity. Phase 1 concluded on 21 November 2025 after working in seven consolidated communities in Tavush, Lori, Vayots Dzor and Syunik.
activities_en: Pasture management plans and 21 pasture infrastructure units
Solar PV and water heaters on public buildings in communities
Support to 31 tourism and related rural businesses; gastro-tourism yards and small production units
196 ha put under sustainable management, including 148 ha of forest
results_en: 508 households received additional income; 31 businesses supported employing about 700 people
Nearly 70,000 visitors benefited from improved infrastructure; over 13,000 people benefited from climate-related initiatives; 102 t CO2 emissions prevented

title_en: Strengthening land based adaptation capacity in communities adjacent to protected areas in Armenia (Adaptation Fund, EPIU)
implementers: Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU) - Implementing Entity
budget_original: Adaptation Fund grant USD 2,506,000 (total project cost USD 2,309,710 + implementing-entity fee USD 196,290)
summary_en: Adaptation Fund project implemented by EPIU to reduce the climate vulnerability of communities next to Khosrov Forest State Reserve (Ararat marz) and Dilijan National Park (Tavush marz). It introduced community-based, climate-smart agricultural practices in degraded areas, strengthened value chains and technology access, and built awareness and monitoring capacity on climate-smart agriculture and land degradation neutrality.
activities_en: Community-based climate-smart agricultural practices in degraded areas and buffer zones (USD 1.73 m)
Value chains and technology transfer for vulnerable rural communities (USD 0.34 m)
Awareness, capacity building, monitoring and decision-making on climate-smart agriculture and LDN (USD 0.2 m)

locations.evidence: Adaptation Fund proposal: Urtsadzor community, in the foothills of the western Ararat valley close to Khosrov Forest State Reserve (Ararat marz); four target communities.
Adaptation Fund proposal: Dilijan, Margahovit and Fioletovo communities near Dilijan National Park in south-western Tavush marz.

title_en: Enhancing the land-based adaptation of communities adjacent to arid zones and forest protected areas of Armenia (Adaptation Fund, EPIU)
implementers: Environmental Project Implementation Unit (EPIU) - Implementing Entity
budget_original: Adaptation Fund grant USD 4,097,546 (USD 833,050 transferred so far)
summary_en: Follow-on Adaptation Fund project executed by EPIU with the Dilijan National Park and Khosrov Forest State Reserve SNCOs. It aims to duplicate and expand the mechanisms of the previous project (Khosrov-Dilijan) for communities adjacent to arid zones and forest protected areas; a search summary adds pasture and irrigation rehabilitation, solar systems, greenhouses and farmer training.
activities_en: Duplicate and expand land-based adaptation mechanisms of the previous Adaptation Fund project
